title: Spokane Insulation Rebates 2026: Avista Pays $1.75 per Square Foot
desc: Spokane insulation rebates for 2026: Avista's $1.75 per square foot for attics, floors and walls, free assessments, no-cost projects in some neighborhoods, and the R-value rules.
lead: Avista pays $1.75 per square foot for attic, floor and wall insulation in Spokane homes that start with thin insulation. Some homes qualify for a project that costs nothing out of pocket.
cards_heading: What insulation rebates pay in Spokane
cards_intro: We read Avista's Home Insulation Program page on October 6, 2026. The program has no income test, and approved installers take the rebate off your bill. Your home must use Avista electricity or natural gas for heating.

cards.title: Attic insulation
cards.note: Your attic must start at R-11 or less and be brought up to R-49 or more. If your space allows it, Avista says you can install R-38 or higher.

cards.title: Floor insulation
cards.note: Floors over a crawl space must start at R-11 or less and reach R-30 or more.

cards.title: Wall insulation
cards.note: For walls with no insulation, brought up to R-11 or more.

cards.title: Duct insulation and sealing
cards.note: $400 per home to insulate ducts that have none and $400 per home to seal ducts.

cards.title: No-cost upgrades for some homes
cards.note: Avista's Home Weatherization Program is free for income-qualifying customers, and some homes in Named Communities can get insulation paid in full.

after_cards:
Working it out

Avista gives its own example: a home with 1,200 square feet of qualifying insulation gets a rebate of about $2,100. That is 1,200 times $1.75. If an attic is 900 square feet and starts at R-11, the attic rebate is 900 times $1.75, or $1,575. Your real amount depends on the area the installer measures and the levels it finds.
sections:
The US Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) says about 68 percent of Spokane homes were built before 1980 and 26 percent before 1940. Only about 16 percent were built in 2000 or later. Older homes are the ones most likely to start under the R-11 line, because building codes asked for little insulation when they were built. About 64 percent of Spokane homes are detached houses and about 59 percent are owner-occupied, which are the homes the program is built for.

Still, being old does not guarantee a rebate. A previous owner may have added insulation. Avista says only 10 to 30 percent of homes in its area qualify based on existing insulation, so the free assessment is the step that tells you.

You call one of Avista's approved installers, who come to your home for a free assessment. They tell you your current R-values, what upgrade is possible, your out-of-pocket cost and the rebate. If you go ahead, they do the work, and the rebate is applied up front. You do not file a form or wait for a check. Avista's list as of July 2026 has ten installers, with names, phone numbers and the services each offers, such as attic, walls, floors, crawl space and duct sealing. Get at least two assessments, because the same job can be priced differently.

You must be an existing Avista residential customer insulating your main home. Single-family houses, duplexes, triplexes and fourplexes count. New construction does not. Avista requires the starting and finished R-values in its tables, so adding an inch to an already insulated attic will not earn the rebate. The Washington table covers homes heated by Avista electricity or natural gas using an electric or gas furnace, a gas boiler, an electric wall heater, radiant heat, baseboards or a heat pump. If you heat with wood or oil, ask Avista before you plan.
claim_heading: How to claim Spokane insulation rebates
claim_steps: Call an approved installer from Avista's Home Insulation Program page for a free assessment.
Ask for the current and new R-values and the price after the rebate in writing.
Ask about no-cost funding for Named Communities and the free Home Weatherization Program if your income may qualify.
Approve the work and let the installer apply the rebate.
Keep the final invoice and the insulation certificate.
faq: How much does Avista pay for attic insulation?
$1.75 per square foot when the attic starts at R-11 or less and ends at R-49 or more.
No for the Home Insulation Program. The Home Weatherization Program is free for income-qualifying customers.
Does my home qualify if I already have some insulation?
Only if it starts at or below the level in Avista's table. Avista says 10 to 30 percent of homes in its area qualify.
Do I fill out a form?
No. Approved installers take the rebate off the bill.
The program page describes installer-based work. Ask Avista if you want to insulate on your own.
